title: List the SKUs held in each warehouse
examObjective: Predicting the result of core DataWeave functions
basics: `groupBy` sorts the elements of an Array into buckets. `payload groupBy $.wh` returns an Object with one key per distinct `wh` value, and each key holds an Array of the elements that had it. `mapObject` then lets you reshape each bucket.
prompt:
The stock system exports `{ sku, wh }` rows. Return an object with one key per warehouse code, each holding the list of SKUs stored there, in their original order.

Warehouse codes were typed in by staff, so the same warehouse may appear as `LDN`, `ldn` or `Ldn`. Use the upper-case code as the key.
hints: Group by the warehouse, then turn each group of rows into a list of SKUs.
The hidden data spells the same warehouse in different cases. What should the grouping key be?
solution:
%dw 2.0
output application/json
---
payload groupBy upper($.wh) mapObject ((rows, wh) -> { (wh): rows.sku })

mustFail.why: groups by the code as typed, so ldn and LDN become two warehouses
mustFail.script:
%dw 2.0
output application/json
---
payload groupBy $.wh mapObject ((rows, wh) -> { (wh): rows.sku })

mustFail.why: stops after groupBy, so each warehouse holds whole rows instead of SKUs

explanation.approach: `groupBy` compares keys exactly, so differently-cased codes make separate buckets. Group on the normalised value. Then `groupBy` alone gives rows; `mapObject` replaces each bucket with the SKUs from it.
